title: Cabinet Approves ₹11,000 Crore Scheme to Build Construction Equipment in India
excerpt: The eight-year scheme offers sales-linked incentives of 13% to 8% to equipment and component makers and up to ₹375 crore for a dedicated testing facility, as more than half of India's roughly ₹1 lakh crore equipment demand is still imported.
body:
• The Union Cabinet has approved a ₹11,000 crore scheme to boost domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment (CIE), to be run by the Ministry of Heavy Industries over eight years from FY2026-27.
  • Sales-linked incentives of 13% to 8% of incremental sales will go to equipment makers and component manufacturers over a five-year disbursement period, after a two-year gestation period.
  • A grant of up to ₹375 crore will fund a dedicated CIE testing facility in India.
  • India's CIE industry is the world's third largest at around ₹97,500 crore in FY2024-25 and is projected to reach around ₹2,28,100 crore by FY2029-30, according to the government.

India will spend ₹11,000 crore to build more of the heavy machines its infrastructure boom runs on at home. The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved the Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem, the government said in a Press Information Bureau release. The scheme, to be implemented by the Ministry of Heavy Industries, will incentivise domestic manufacturing of CIE and its components and establish a dedicated CIE testing facility in the country.

The equipment in scope is the technologically advanced end of the market: ship-to-shore cranes, tunnel boring machines, hydraulic excavators and off-highway trucks, among others. Briefing the media, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said demand for such equipment in India is around ₹1 lakh crore and more than half of it is still imported, ANI reported. The scheme is expected to attract investments worth ₹21,000 crore, enable import substitution worth ₹22,500 crore and increase exports to around four times their current level, according to ANI's report of the briefing.

"Today, the requirement in India is around 1 lakh crore. And more than half of it is still imported; this import needs to be reduced so that it is manufactured in India itself."

— Ashwini Vaishnaw, Union Minister

How the money flows

The scheme runs for eight years from FY2026-27: a two-year gestation period (FY2026-27 to FY2027-28) for setting up manufacturing facilities, a five-year incentive disbursement period (FY2028-29 to FY2032-33), and a final year (FY2033-34) to settle incentives on incremental sales of FY2032-33, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. It has two components. The first is a sales-linked incentive on the incremental sales value of eligible equipment and components, paid to approved applicants in two categories — eligible OEMs and component manufacturers — at graded rates from 13% to 8% over five years. The second is a grant of up to ₹375 crore, as viability gap funding, for a dedicated CIE testing facility.

Why now

India's CIE industry is currently the world's third largest, after China and the United States, with a market size of around ₹97,500 crore in FY2024-25. Driven by growth in infrastructure — roads and ports — and housing, it is projected to more than double to around ₹2,28,100 crore by FY2029-30, according to the government release. The government said fostering indigenous manufacturing would ensure supply chain security, increase employment opportunities and promote Atmanirbhar Bharat, positioning India as a key player in the global CIE market.

What to watch next is the scheme's operating detail: which equipment and component categories are notified as eligible, which manufacturers are approved, and where the testing facility is set up. Those decisions will determine how much of the ₹11,000 crore reaches the tunnel boring machines and cranes that Indian projects currently source from abroad.
